headline_marked: [[AI-generated posters]] can be more than repetitive
headline: AI-generated posters can be more than repetitive
summary: ChatGPT can produce a wide array of distinct design styles, moving beyond generic AI art to create unique visuals for events.
details: AI-generated posters often suffer from a repetitive, identikit style that can become visually tiresome. This article explores how to break free from this monotony.

By specifying design aesthetics beyond the default, users can prompt AI models like ChatGPT to generate posters with unique visual identities. Examples include "modernist / Bauhaus-influenced graphic style" or "contemporary editorial" looks.
The author experimented with ChatGPT, initially requesting a "clean, unfussy, bright layout with a bold striking spring-themed graphic." While better than generic AI art, it still felt too familiar.

A second prompt, asking for a "completely different design aesthetic," yielded more distinctive results. ChatGPT suggested a range of styles, from "Bauhaus / Modernist" and "Swiss Style" to more avant-garde options like "Brutalist Graphic Design" and "90s Rave Flyer."

These diverse styles, including "Risograph Print Style," "Cut Paper / Collage," and "Japanese Minimal Poster," demonstrate AI's potential to create visually engaging and non-repetitive event materials, moving beyond the common AI art tropes.
